items.title: vLLM Delivers Day-0 Support for Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary_1line: vLLM supports Kimi K3.1 Pro on day 0: sparse attention on a KDA hybrid, a packed KV cache with FP8 or NVFP4 latents and MXFP4 index keys, token-sharded prefill, decode context parallelism, and fused low-latency decode.

editorial.tldr: Moonshot launched Kimi K3.1 Pro on Oct 27 with a botched rollout that forced an apology and restored user quotas. It then published the full weights on Hugging Face in early November, and vLLM, Huawei Ascend and Moore Threads shipped day-zero support, followed by a Coder variant sized at 775 GB.
editorial.whats_new: Wccftech reports on Nov 16 that Alibaba's new Qwen4-Max does not overtake Kimi K3.1 Pro, despite matching its parameter count at a lower price, so K3.1 Pro stays the open-weight reference point.
editorial.why_it_matters: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8T-parameter open-weight model with day-zero vLLM support and hosted endpoints on NEAR AI Cloud, ZenMux and Verda, so teams can run it in-house or via third parties instead of depending on Moonshot's own quota-limited service.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before routing production traffic to Kimi K3.1 Pro, read the licence's commercial conditions and pin a vLLM release with its day-zero support, and keep a second host as fallback given the botched launch.

status.detail: Weights are public under a commercial licence with conditions; serving, hardware and fine-tuning support has followed, and the newest item is a rival-model comparison, not new Moonshot news.
